items.title: CSIR-CCMB team identifies potential new targets to fight Tuberculosis
points: The discovery is particularly significant for India, which accounts for nearly a quarter of global TB cases and about a third of drug-resistant infections, according to the World Health Organisation’s Global TB Report 2025.
Led by CCMB Director Vinay Kumar Nandicoori, the research team mapped the protein export machinery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the bacterium responsible for TB.

The research was carried out by joint first authors Priyadarshini Sanyal and Jagadeeshwari Uppada in collaboration with scientists from the Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai, led by Areejit Samal, and the Translational Health Science and…

Using a combination of computational modelling and laboratory experiments, the researchers identified 92 key components and nearly 200 molecular reactions involved in the bacterium’s protein transport network.
These included the general Sec pathway, the Twin-Arginine Translocation (Tat) system and the specialised ESX secretion systems unique to this group of bacteria.
The team focused on two major secretion pathways, SecA1 and Tat, employing CRISPR-based gene-silencing technology to reduce their activity.

items.title: Regulator caps charges for internet-based links between telecom networks, pushes for phasing out of older port technology
points: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) on Monday capped the fees telecom companies can charge each other for internet-based (IP) connections between their networks.

Under the Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026, an operator may charge no more than ₹5.6 lakh per year for a 1 Gbps IP port and ₹42.3 lakh per year for a 10 Gbps port.
The rules on these charges were framed in 2001 and last revised in 2012, when networks ran on older E1/TDM circuit technology.
The notification goes with a separate amendment, the Telecommunication Interconnection (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026, which also takes effect on January 1.
The regulation redefines “port” to include IP ports, measured in Mbps or Gbps, as well as the legacy E1 port at 2.048 Mbps.
For port sizes other than 1 Gbps and 10 Gbps, the operator providing the port must work out the charge transparently, using the same method TRAI used.

items.title: 60% of the ethanol offered to OMCs this year is maize-based
points: Ethanol producers have offered 19.32 billion litres against the oil marketing companies’ (OMCs) tender requirement of 11 billion litres for the 2026-27 supply year, with maize-based ethanol accounting for nearly 60% of the total offers.
The quantity offered is close to India’s officially confirmed distillation capacity of 19.5 billion litres, indicating that almost the entire capacity has been offered for ethanol production.
Of the 19.32 billion litres offered in the tender, 11.45 billion litres is maize-based ethanol.
This is significant because maize production is estimated by industry experts to be around 15% lower than the previous year when it stood at 55 million tonnes.

items.title: Shah sets Dec 2028 deadline for Gujarat, 2029 for India to go drug-free
points: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday set a December 31, 2028, deadline to make Gujarat drug-free, a year ahead of the Centre’s target for a drug-free India, and announced a toll-free helpline to enable citizens to report drug-related activities.
The helpline, 1033, will become operational from December 1, Shah said while addressing a gathering in Ahmedabad.
“After a ‘Naxal-free India’, the Modi government now aims at creating a ‘Drug-free India’ by December 31, 2029.
Since Prime Minister Narendra Modi and I both hail from Gujarat, we intend to make Gujarat drug-free earlier, by December 31, 2028,” Shah said.
Shah was in Ahmedabad to inaugurate and lay the foundation stones for development projects worth around ₹1,400 crore.
These included projects worth ₹1,024 crore through the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation and another ₹400 crore through the Gujarat government’s Roads and Buildings Department and the Centre.

items.title: Traders body led by BJP MP to seek alternative sites for political stirs
points: The Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT) has called a national meeting to seek designated sites for political protests and demonstrations on the outskirts of cities, arguing that prolonged agitations in commercial areas disrupt business and affect the…

The traders’ body, led by BJP lawmaker Praveen Khandelwal, will meet in the national Capital on November 13 to discuss the proposal at a national meeting that will include senior trade leaders from across the country.
In a press release issued by Khandelwal, the body said they plan to approach the government and can even go to the court to push for designated protest venues.
“Suitable locations should be designated on the outskirts of every city, or at other appropriate places, for protests and demonstrations,” said Khandelwal, the Chandni Chowk MP.
The lNDIA bloc also organised a mega rally at the Ramlila maidan on November 1.

items.title: BJP accuses Kharge of appeasement over Eid remark; Congress hits back
points: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday accused Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge of appeasement politics and hurting Hindu sentiments by calling Diwali the “Eid of happiness”.
Extending his Diwali greetings over the weekend, Kharge had told reporters that Diwali is a major festival celebrated by everyone in India and described it as ‘khushiyon ka Eid’.

Why is it that when it comes to Diwali, which has its own sanctity, tradition and identity, you choose to call it Eid while extending greetings to Hindus?” questioned BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia on Monday, alleging that the Congress sought to…
Congress leader Pawan Khera countered that Eid was often used as a metaphor for joy.
Eid means ‘tyohar’, Diwali ka ‘tyohar’, Holi ka ‘tyohar’ - that’s what he means.” Congress leader Rashid Alvi made the same point.

items.title: HC backs denial of entry to OCIs involved in sexual offences
points: The Delhi high court has held that the Centre is empowered to deny an overseas citizen of India (OCI) card holder entry into India if it receives information indicating that the person is a convicted child sex offender in a foreign country.
The court delivered the verdict while hearing the case of a man of Indian origin who held a foreign passport and an OCI card.

Upon arriving at Indira Gandhi International Airport, New Delhi, on January 7, 2026, he was served with an order denying him permission to enter India and directing him to depart on the first available flight.
His counsel argued that the order was non-speaking, failed to disclose specific reasons or grounds for refusing entry, and merely referred to him as a registered child sex offender.
The counsel further submitted that proceedings against the man had been initiated in the United States in 2019, culminating in a no-contest plea in October 2022.

items.title: Sugar prices remain high despite a fourfold rise in production
points: According to data released by the Indian Sugar and Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA), sugar production in India reached 1.285 million tonnes as of November 5, while it was 320,000 tonnes during the corresponding period last year.
However, domestic sugar prices continued to remain elevated, with the average modal retail price at ₹60 per kg on Monday, up 36% from ₹44 per kg a year ago.
The average modal price was also higher than the ₹55 per kg recorded a month ago, according to data from the Department of Consumer Affairs (DOCA).

Maharashtra accounted for 1.078 million tonnes of sugar production, with 136 mills operational as of November 5, compared with 123,000 tonnes produced by 101 mills during the corresponding period last year.
Seven mills in Tamil Nadu have produced 64,000 tonnes, while 12 mills in Gujarat and three in Telangana have also started operations.

items.title: The great global paradox: Unprecedented progress, unresolved problems
points: The most important challenge of our age is that human capacity to address problems has expanded significantly even as our commitment to working collectively remains inadequate.
Human ingenuity is able to build machines far more intelligent than human beings.
The crises associated with the wars in Ukraine, Gaza, and Yemen have demonstrated the devastating human impact of a global order unable to prevent conflict or work towards protecting civilian life.
The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees recorded that 123.2 million people were forcibly displaced around the world at the end of 2024.

The International Labour Organization’s 2026 Youth Employment Report estimated that more than 257 million young people were not in a position to receive employment, education, training, or capacity-building in 2025.

The responsibility of governments ought to be to rebuild the transition from learning to livelihoods through meaningful education, quality apprenticeships leading to job opportunities, credible recruitment, and institutional support for promoting…

items.title: IIT Hyderabad's Forward Deployed Engineering Programme To Begin On December 5
points: The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Hyderabad is offering a three-month programme in Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) for professionals who want to learn how to build and use Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems in real-world situations.
The online programme will begin on December 5 and will include 52 sessions conducted by IIT Hyderabad faculty members.
Interested candidates can register through the official website, ailaunchpad.cse.iith.ac.in.
The course will focus on taking AI projects beyond the testing stage and making them useful in everyday business and organisational work.
The programme will include practical exercises, AI project development, research sessions by IIT Hyderabad faculty members and webinars with industry professionals.
The programme will be led by Praveen Tammana, Ashish Mishra, Anupam Sanghi and Abhijit Das from IIT Hyderabad's Department of Computer Science and Engineering.
Those who complete the programme and meet the required conditions will receive a certificate from IIT Hyderabad.

items.title: 3 New Skoda Kylaqs For India
points: Skoda Kylaq is one of the popular SUVs that the brand has launched in the Indian market.
This sub-4-metre SUV is so popular that Skoda has sold over 50,000 units of the Kylaq since November 2024.
The CNG version will continue to use the same 1.0-litre turbo-petrol engine that generates 115 PS and 178 Nm of torque.
It remains to be seen whether Skoda will retune the engine for efficiency or offer the Kylaq CNG with the same power and torque figures as the petrol version, like the Mahindra XUV 3XO ZNG.
Skoda is currently evaluating whether it can actually offer the Kylaq with the larger 1.5-litre TSI engine with a manual or DSG transmission option.

items.title: Red Fort blast a year on: Families still waiting for justice and closure
points: A year after the deadly blast near Delhi’s Red Fort claimed 12 lives, the families of those killed are still struggling to rebuild their lives, grappling with financial uncertainty, the absence of loved ones and questions about justice.
The November 10, 2025, explosion took place at the junction in front of Red Fort.
Those killed included Amar Kataria, Vinay Pathak, Ashok Kumar, Mohammad Lukman, Lokesh Kumar, Jumman Mohammed, Dinesh Kumar Mishra, Numan Ansari, Mohsin Malik, Pankaj Saini and Bilal Ahmad Sangoo.
For Ashok Kumar’s wife, Sonam Devi, 26, the tragedy meant leaving Delhi and moving back to her parents’ home in Amroha, Uttar Pradesh.
Of the ₹10 lakh compensation she received from the Delhi government, she said ₹5 lakh was taken by Ashok’s family.
Guddu has brought Dinesh’s 13-year-old son to Delhi and enrolled him in a boarding school in west Delhi.
For 50-year-old Imraan, from Uttar Pradesh’s Shamli district, the loss of his 21-year-old son Noman came when his elder son was already undergoing a kidney transplant.

items.title: Rights panel seeks report from LSGD on linking Chilavannur Bund Road with Vyttila-Aroor bypass
points: All bottlenecks in linking the crucial road corridor with the NH bypass by widening a narrow 200-metre-long stretch must be cleared on an urgent basis, considering the necessity to streamline traffic flow, he ordered.
However, the delay in widening the 200-metre narrow stretch hampered its extension to the NH bypass at Thykoodam.

After registering a suo motu case, the Commission, at a sitting on October 17, issued an order directing that the stalled work resume to extend the road eastward and realise its potential to decongest S.A.

A representative of the District Collector, the superintending engineer of the Kochi Corporation, and the town planner of the Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA) were among those who attended the sitting.
The GCDA, which owns bund road, submitted that ₹15 crore was needed to acquire 60 cents of land for the extension.
Another ₹5 crore was required to complete the extension work.

items.title: SDPI takes lead in campaign for Tirur district through Malappuram bifurcation
points: The Social Democratic Party of India (SDPI) is leading a campaign for the bifurcation of Malappuram district, demanding the formation of a new district with Tirur as its headquarters.
The party will form a human chain from the Malappuram Collectorate to Tirur on January 26, 2027, Republic Day.

Though parties like the Congress, Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), Welfare Party of India, and the CPI(M) have supported the demand for bifurcation on administrative grounds, the SDPI is the only party to have proposed a specific district structure with…
The SDPI has been demanding Tirur district since 2010 and has organised several protests.
According to figures presented by its leaders, Malappuram had a population of 41.12 lakh in the 2011 Census, while Idukki, Wayanad, Pathanamthitta, and Alappuzha together had 52.51 lakh.
The party puts the bus availability in Malappuram at three per one lakh people, against 20 in Idukki and Pathanamthitta and 29 in Wayanad.
